name: אֶלְקָנָה
gloss: God has acquired; or God has made
summary: Above all Elkanah of Ramathaim-zophim, the Levite of Ephraim's hill country, husband of Hannah and Peninnah and father of Samuel, who went up yearly to worship and sacrifice to Yahweh of armies at Shiloh (1Sa 1:1–3, 19–20). The name is also borne by a son of Korah (Exo 6:24) and other Levites of Korah's line in the genealogies of 1Ch 6, a Levite ancestor of Berechiah among those who returned (1Ch 9:16), a Korahite who joined David at Ziklag (1Ch 12:7), a doorkeeper for the ark (1Ch 15:23), and the second to king Ahaz, killed by Zichri of Ephraim (2Ch 28:7). The name is אֵל “God” with the verb קָנָה, “God has acquired”, the God who is קֹנֵה of heaven and earth (Gen 14:19) and who acquired his people (Exo 15:16; Deu 32:6); or, with the Ugaritic sense, “God has made (a son)”, as Eve said at Cain's birth, “I have gotten a man with Yahweh” (Gen 4:1). Scripture does not explain the name.

evidence.note: “There was a man of Ramathaim-zophim … and his name was אֶלְקָנָה son of Jeroham.”
Hannah bore Samuel to Elkanah: “because I asked him of Yahweh”.
Heman the singer, “son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham”.
“The sons of Korah: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph.”
Elkanah among the Korahites who came to David at Ziklag.
“Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark.”
Zichri killed “Elkanah, the second to the king”.
“God Most High, קֹנֵה of heaven and earth”: אֵל with the participle of the same verb.
“Is he not your father who acquired you? He made you and established you.”
“I have gotten (קָנִיתִי) a man with Yahweh.”

note: TIPNR's keys use English verse numbers (1Ch.6.25, 6.26, 12.6); the evidence cites the Hebrew (1Ch 6:10–11, 12:7). Not checked which of the 1Ch 6 Elkanahs TIPNR assigns to which record beyond its keys; Elkanah of 1Ch 6:12 and 6:19 (Eng 6:27, 34) is Samuel's father, filed under Elkanah@1Sa.1.1.
